title: random
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to use random for chance events, with seed(1) so your practice rolls stay the same.
idea: The random module picks chance values for games. In these lessons we call random.seed(1) first, so the random numbers stay the same every time you press Run. That keeps checking your answers fair. random.randint(1, 6) rolls a dice from 1 to 6.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the label on the third roll to Roll 3: and press Run. The numbers should stay 2, 5, 1 because of the seed.

practice.text: Import random, seed(1), print two dice rolls 1 to 6.
practice.hint: Fill both empty print() lines with random.randint(1, 6). Keep random.seed(1) so your rolls match the lesson.
practice.starterTip: Try print(random.randint(1, 6)) twice. With seed(1), expect 2 then 5.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if seed(1) and two randint(1,6) prints show 2 then 5.

practice.text: seed(1). Use random.choice on ['a','b','c'] twice and print both.
practice.hint: Make a list like letters = ["a", "b", "c"], and then print random.choice(letters) on each blank line.
practice.starterTip: Example: print(random.choice(["a", "b", "c"])) twice. With seed(1), output should be a then c.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if outputs are a then c with seed(1).

quiz.question: Why call random.seed(1) in lessons?

options.text: So rolls match every Run for checking

quiz.correct: Right, a fixed seed makes practice predictable.

quiz.question: What does random.randint(1, 6) return?
quiz.wrong: It is a dice friendly range.

quiz.question: Does seed change after you set it once?

options.text: Later randint calls advance the sequence

quiz.correct: Right, the sequence is fixed but it keeps moving forward.
quiz.wrong: With seed(1) the first rolls are 2, 5, 1.

project.title: Dice Roller
project.desc: Use seed(1). Print five dice rolls labeled Roll 1 to Roll 5.
project.starter:
import random
random.seed(1)
for i in range(1, 6):
    print()
